builds.name: Reference: Range and poke
builds.goal: Reference for Ziggs: establish a repeatable reference
builds.hypothesis: An artillery siege mage who combines ranged explosives with periodic empowered attacks and turret execution. Separate ability poke from the periodic empowered real attack and tower execution. Lich Bane needs a safe attack; siege results do not establish better champion-duel output. Range-compatible spell hits test poke AP/penetration before a commitment.
builds.summary: Range-compatible spell hits test poke AP/penetration before a commitment.
testPlan: Kit question for Ziggs: Separate ability poke from the periodic empowered real attack and tower execution. Lich Bane needs a safe attack; siege results do not establish better champion-duel output.

Start with the early core (Luden, then Horizon) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Use this as the control for the other three routes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Range-compatible spell hits test poke AP/penetration before a commitment. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern.

Q evidence: Ziggs throws a bouncing bomb that deals magic damage. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.

builds.name: Short Fuse siege cycle
builds.summary: Reduce passive cooldown through casts and deliver repeated structure attacks.
builds.goal: Reduce passive cooldown through casts and deliver repeated structure attacks.
builds.hypothesis: Short Fuse's AP magic packet is multiplied against structures and casts reduce its cooldown. Lich Bane tests spell-followed structure attacks; Nashor supports actual attack cadence while Hullbreaker rewards fifth attacks and nearby siege minions. W destroys towers only after the specified health threshold.
testPlan: Required state: A reachable tower, tracked passive/Spellblade cooldowns, wave present and W threshold recorded.
Log tower damage after spaced casts and every fifth attack, separating Short Fuse, Lich Bane and Hullbreaker.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Defenders force retreat before attacks and delaying mana or penetration loses wave control.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Short Fuse's structure multiplier is not automatically applied to item damage.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Lich Bane, Nashor's Tooth, Hullbreaker, Rabadon's Deathcap, Zhonya's Hourglass, Berserker's Greaves. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Satchel mine path
builds.summary: Force a mine crossing before landing the center of R.
builds.goal: Force a mine crossing before landing the center of R.
builds.hypothesis: W knocks enemies away and E mines slow for a finite ten-second area. Directed W can move a target across E and delay escape from R's center, which deals more than its edge. Bloodletter tests magic damage ramp, Cosmic supports repositioning and Liandry asks for retained damage contact.
testPlan: Required state: Mines placed on the expected knockback path and R center aimed at the resulting position.
Count mine damage packets and center/edge R hits with W knockback through versus away from E.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Incorrect W direction clears the target away from mines or R delay permits escape.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: E primary description states successive mine detonations on one target deal reduced damage, so do not sum full packets.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Blackfire Torch, Liandry's Torment, Bloodletter's Curse, Cosmic Drive, Rabadon's Deathcap, Sorcerer's Shoes. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
